facts.text: The hotel is at 1 Princes Street in Edinburgh, where the Old Town meets the New Town.
facts.excerpt: The Balmoral, 1 Princes Street, where Old Town meets New

facts.text: Guests are welcomed with bespoke Balmoral tartan and classic Scottish art.
facts.excerpt: A welcome in bespoke Balmoral tartan; Hebridean blues, heather hues and classic Scottish art

facts.text: The suites' design, by Olga Polizzi, takes its cue from the Scottish landscape.
facts.excerpt: The design, as envisioned by Olga Polizzi, embodies the Scottish landscape.

facts.text: SCOTCH, the hotel's whisky bar, holds over 500 Scottish whiskies in a hand-crafted, oak-panelled cabinet.
facts.excerpt: With over 500 unique varieties of Scottish whisky within the bar’s hand-crafted, oak-panelled whisky cabinet

facts.text: At SCOTCH, Whisky Ambassadors guide guests through whisky tastings.
facts.excerpt: your knowledgeable Whisky Ambassador will guide you through the fundamentals of Scotch Whisky

facts.text: Number One holds four AA Rosettes, is Michelin Guide-recommended and is included in La Liste.
facts.excerpt: Number One currently holds four AA Rosettes, is Michelin Guide-recommended, and is included in the prestigious La Liste

facts.text: Number One serves honeycomb harvested from the hotel's rooftop hives.
facts.excerpt: Delicate honeycomb harvested from our rooftop hives.

facts.text: Number One offers three- and five-course tasting menus built on Scottish ingredients.
facts.excerpt: Our three and five-course tasting menus honour the character and abundance of Scottish ingredients.

facts.text: The Palm Court serves afternoon tea under palm trees, a glass dome and a Venetian chandelier.
facts.excerpt: Take a seat under the green leaves of palm trees, gently bathed in the light that cascades down from the sparkling glass dome and the Venetian chandelier.

facts.text: At the Palm Court, loose-leaf teas are poured at the table.
facts.excerpt: loose-leaf teas (pleasingly poured tableside)

facts.text: Brasserie Prince pairs classic French cooking with Scottish produce.
facts.excerpt: Brasserie Prince celebrates the very best of Scottish produce with classic French cooking.

facts.text: Bar Prince has cornflower-blue leather chairs and a bar with copper barware.
facts.excerpt: Take a seat in one of the cornflower-blue leather chairs or perch at the bar, festooned with gleaming copper barware

facts.text: The Irene Forte Spa has an indoor lap pool.
facts.excerpt: An indoor lap pool

facts.text: The spa has a sauna and steam room.
facts.excerpt: Sauna and steam room

facts.text: The spa has a gym equipped with Technogym.
facts.excerpt: A state-of-the-art gym with the latest Technogym

facts.text: The Irene Forte Spa draws its inspiration from Sicily.
facts.excerpt: Irene Forte Spa brings the soul of Sicily into the rhythms of the city

facts.text: Castle View junior suites look out to Edinburgh Castle on Castle Rock, an extinct volcano.
facts.excerpt: looking out towards the rugged castle on the 700-million-year-old extinct volcano, Castle Rock.

facts.text: Family Rooms are two interconnecting rooms with two bedrooms.
facts.excerpt: Our interconnecting rooms create a relaxing stay for families, with two bedrooms

facts.text: The Bowes-Lyon Suite is named for the Queen Mother, a former patron of the hotel.
facts.excerpt: Named for and inspired by former patron of The Balmoral, The Queen Mother, born Elizabeth Bowes-Lyon

facts.text: J.K. Rowling finished the final Harry Potter book in the suite now named after her.
facts.excerpt: the J.K. Rowling suite, where the infamous author finished the final book in the series

facts.text: The hotel was built in 1902 for the North British Railway company.
facts.excerpt: This hotel was originally built in 1902 for the North British Railway company

facts.text: The hotel's clock tower is set three minutes fast so people don't miss their trains.
facts.excerpt: clock tower is set three minutes fast so guests and railway passengers don't miss their trains

facts.text: During Hogmanay the clock marks the turning of the year precisely on time.
facts.excerpt: During Hogmanay, the city's New Year celebrations, it marks the turning of the year precisely on time.

facts.text: Kilted doormen welcome guests at the entrance.
facts.excerpt: classic kilted doormen welcoming guests

facts.text: A harpist plays from the balcony in the Palm Court.
facts.excerpt: The Palm Court, where a harpist plays from the balcony

facts.text: The Old Town and the Royal Mile are just on the other side of Waverley station.
facts.excerpt: the picture-perfect Old Town (and home to the Royal Mile, the heart of Edinburgh since the Middle Ages and street upon which many landmarks lie), is just on the other side of Waverley

facts.text: In Gaelic, the word balmoral translates as majestic dwelling.
facts.excerpt: In Gaelic, the word "balmoral" translates to “majestic dwelling”

facts.text: Number One is Michelin-starred, with chef Mathew Sherry.
facts.excerpt: At the Michelin-starred Number One, chef Mathew Sherry turns fine Scottish ingredients into creative, seasonal dishes

facts.text: The spa and fitness center received a major facelift, reopening for summer 2025 guests.
facts.excerpt: The spa and fitness center just received a major facelift. Summer 2025 guests will be among the first to enjoy the gorgeous new space

facts.text: The hotel has 10 event spaces.
facts.excerpt: our 10 events spaces offer style, comfort and world-class service

facts.text: The hotel calls itself an Edinburgh icon at an unparalleled address.
facts.excerpt: An Edinburgh Icon at an Unparalleled Address.

facts.text: There is no dress code, but sportswear, shorts and beach shoes are discouraged in the restaurants.
facts.excerpt: refrain from wearing sportswear, shorts and beach shoes in our restaurants
